tess: Heads up — seeing sustained page-stall spikes on Mistral runs with long contexts (>32k). KV cache residency jumps, allocator shows frequent page reclaim. Attached telemetry: grafana/internal/kv/series?id=kv_page_faults

devon: repro steps? what workload / model config?

tess: repro is the convo-history benchmark (mixed user traffic, ~60% long-turns). Model= mistral-mqa-2b, rope_scale=1.25, kv_page_size=64k, batcher=max_tokens=1024. Spikes start after ~8k tokens in a session.

ryan: saw something similar last month on a streaming job. growth only after rope rescale triggers, page churn goes up. suspect fragmentation + partial writes.

marie: which kernel is runtime picking for those ops? could be falling back to generic matmul and thrashing memory.

alex: quick check: `curl -s $ADMIN/api/runtime/selection?model=mistral-mqa-2b` shows kernel_selector -> fallback: matmul_generic_v1 for sequence_len > 8192.

infra-bot: Deploy 2134567901 by devon: runtime/selector: add debug logging for kernel hints

devon: added a tiny trace patch to log selected kernel + kv page allocations in-flight. pushed to canary. can run repro with `make repro-convo TRACE=1`

tess: pasted perf output from canary (snip):
```
kv_pages_in_use=342176
kv_page_faults_per_sec=48
scheduler_stall_ms=140
hot_kernel=matmul_generic_v1
cold_kernel=matmul_optimized_v2
heap_frag_percent=22
`

devon: interesting — hot kernel is generic while optimized is available. kernel_selector is preferring the generic because of batcher heuristic that assumes large seqs -> single large kernel for throughput. That seems to degrade locality for KV writes.

ryan: hypothesis: large-kernel path writes KV pages in big sweeps that interleave with GC leading to partial slab holes. When rope_scale bumps, some slots shift and we do many small updates inside big page ranges -> fragmentation.

marie: quick mitigation ideas: 1) prefer optimized v2 for MQA when kv_pages_in_use > 100k; 2) reduce kv_sweep_interval from 10s -> 2s for affected canary; 3) enable kv_compact_on_idle to coalesce.

alex: for immediate repro runs, try forcing kernel hint: `export REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINT=matmul_optimized_v2` and run `make repro-convo`. If that reduces scheduler_stall_ms -> good signal.

devon: forced run results: scheduler_stall_ms down from 140 -> 30, kv_page_faults_per_sec down 48 -> 6. Looks promising.

tess: ok can we ship a targeted change: tweak selector to prefer optimized_v2 when model contains "mqa" OR seq_len_distribution.p90 > 12k. Also add telemetry counter for "kv_fragmentation_events".

ryan: agree. I'll prototype kernel hint change + a small batching heuristic: if avg_seq_len > 8k then switch to streaming batch path (smaller kernels, more granular KV writes). Should reduce fragmentation.

devon: I'll add a short-lived CI job that runs the convo benchmark for 2h with the selector tweak and collect pprof + pmap every 5m.

marie: also add a guard: if mem_frag > 30% then trigger kv_compact_on_oom=1 and alert on #eng-runtime.

tess: nice. Next steps: devon run canary with selector tweak, ryan test batcher change in feature branch, marie add compacting guard + alert rules. If all green, rollout to dedicated and then to hosted with rollback window 1h. :thumbsup:

alex: note for release notes: "Mitigate KV fragmentation under rope-scaling for MQA models; improved kernel selection and batching heuristics."

infra-bot: Issue created: INFRA-1423 — kv fragmentation telemetry + selector tweak (assignee=devon)

devon: starting the canary now, will post logs to the thread.

tess: thanks — please ping when the canary completes or if you see regressions.
